DEVSNITCHER FULL-SURFACE TEST HARNESS

Serve this fixture with python -m http.server 8000 and open http://localhost:8000/devsnitcher-full-surface.html. It deliberately generates console, network, and JavaScript failures on demand so one real SNITCH run exercises every report surface.

Controls

Live sequence

  1. Open this harness.
  2. Press ARM 3s.
  3. Immediately open DEVSnitcher.
  4. Press SNITCH.
  5. Do not click outside the DEVSnitcher popup.
  6. Allow the armed harness to fire: one burst at 3s, then an attempt every 2s up to 10 real fires (a tick blocked by a previous burst is retried), so evidence keeps flowing while acquisition runs.
  7. Wait for DEVSnitcher to finish.
  8. COPY SNITCHSHOT.
  9. Paste the report into your AI of choice.

User Description is never fabricated here — it is supplied through DEVSnitcher’s notes field before SNITCH.

The manual TRIGGER ALL button remains for debugging. It closes the DEVSnitcher popup when clicked, so it is not part of the live-acceptance procedure. ARM 3s exists because the popup must stay open while acquisition runs: it fires once after 3 seconds, then repeats the same trigger every 2 seconds up to 10 times, so a SNITCH pressed anywhere in that window always overlaps live evidence, and the firing log timestamps each burst for the acceptance record.

Network failures this harness generates

SurfaceWhat fires
HTTP failure GET /devsnitcher-intentional-404-<nonce>.txt → HTTP 404
Transport failure GET http://127.0.0.1:9/refuse-now → connection refused
Delayed transport failure GET http://127.0.0.1:9/refuse-delayed after ~600 ms → connection refused

The acceptance bar: the pasted SNITCHSHOT’s Network section must contain at least one real failed request, and the Summary must not read 0 failed API requests.

Distinctive snapshot / DOM target

DEVSNITCHER HARNESS TARGET

This element has the stable id #devsnitcher-harness-target and data attributes so the report’s DOM Context and screenshots are recognizably this page.

Status marker: data-devset="full-surface"

What TRIGGER ALL produces

  • Console: log, info, warn, error, debug, a warning reporting the intentional 404, a delayed console error (~900 ms).
  • JavaScript: an unhandled Promise rejection and an uncaught runtime exception.
  • Network: one 404, one connection-refused, one delayed connection-refused (~600 ms).
  • Focus: moves to the harness target so the DOM snapshot is distinctive.
